correctness.rationale: The exact physical normalization is correct and denominator strictly positive for 1<k<e. Differentiation proves a global one-step image inside the strictly increasing interval [0,1), so no nonfixed cycles and all orbits converge. The growth ratio has a single strict maximum, fixing the exact 0/1/2-positive-root alternatives. Its explicit decreasing-branch preimage gives all initial-data basins. At the fold, the second derivative is -c/(1-c), giving the universal n(t_n-c)->2(1-c)/c above c; the Lambert-W inverse branch yields the exact square-root basin-length coefficient. Invariant probabilities must be fixed-atom mixtures by dominated convergence. A standalone standard-library script passed its finite diagnostic checks.

value.rationale: This is a natural all-initial density persistence problem for a published population map: excess crowding also causes extinction despite positive attractors. It determines exact lower and upper global thresholds and quantifies a discontinuous fold onset of the active basin together with a critical \(n^{-1}\) clock, on an open two-parameter sector. This is not just a numerical table, a redrawing of local bifurcations, or a narrow arbitrary parameter value; the precise cutoffs are potentially useful for finite-density viability studies.
